title: Quarterly roadmap: Autoscale fallback reservoirs, canary cadence, and cost-hedge experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and sequence a quarterly roadmap that operationalizes a multi-tier fallback strategy for Dedicated capacity autoscaling. This ticket captures the product plan to introduce: 1) reservoir (pre-warmed) pools for graceful surge handling, 2) canary cadence and rollout windows tied to predictive signals, 3) cross-region surge choreography and regional fallback priority, and 4) a set of cost-hedge experiments (fractional reservations, short-term burst credits).

Why this matters: Customers running latency-sensitive workloads require predictable SLAs during unexpected spikes. Current Dedicated pools can be brittle under correlated surges (e.g., product launches). The roadmap is intended to reduce P95 latency regressions during surge by 40% while keeping attributable cost uplift <6% in production.

Deliverables (quarter):
- Product spec for reservoir architecture (pool sizing heuristics, eviction policy, UI controls)
- Canary cadence playbook (criteria, automation steps, rollback triggers)
- Cost-hedge experiment matrix and measurement plan (metrics, dashboards, guardrails)
- Runbook for ops + SRE for surge / fallback events
- Stakeholder alignment and launch checklist (billing, sales comms, legal if needed)
acceptance_criteria: Spec approved: Reservoir API + Console controls reviewed and accepted by Eng and SRE
Canary playbook validated in lab with at least 3 surge scenarios and documented rollback thresholds
Cost hedging experiments defined and instrumentation complete (per-token cost, reservoir utilization, P95 latency)
Dashboard panels added to Console: reservoir utilization, failover rate, per-region fallback activations
Runbook published in Confluence and ops drill scheduled and executed
updates: 2026-02-02 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and aligned initial scope with SRE and Infra PMs. Goal to slot work across Q2 planning. Asked Eng to provide rough cost model by 2026-02-10.

2026-02-05 - Miguel Ramos: Kickoff with Runtime leads. Decided to model two reservoir flavors: short-burst (minutes) and sustained-warm (hours). Eng to prototype sizing heuristic (alpha) by 2026-02-19.
2026-02-07 - Claire Zhang (SRE): Shared failure modes from Nov 2025 incident; recommended adding per-customer fallback priority and a soft-throttle early-warning signal from admission controller.

2026-02-09 - Product review: Trade-offs discussed - aggressive pre-warming reduces cold-start latency but raises committed cost. We agreed on conservative default sizing with admin-visible scaling multiplier and cost alerts.

2026-02-11 - Miguel Ramos: Eng spike started (prototype of reservoir allocator). Linked PR for allocator simulator: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3392. Early sim shows 28% P95 improvement in synthetic surge with 4% cost increase (alpha config).

2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Updated roadmap draft and shared with Growth/Support for downstream comms. Added 'billing opt-in' requirement and flagged need for legal review if we introduce prepaid burst credits.
risks: Committed cost creep if reservoir heuristics are too conservative
Complexity in cross-region choreography could introduce new failure modes (split-brain routing during network partitions)
Customer confusion without clear UI/quotas could lead to support churn
mitigations: Start with pilot customers via feature flag and Billing opt-in; instrument per-customer cost and utilization metrics
Implement safe defaults and automated rollback triggers for canaries (latency and error-rate thresholds)
Ship clear Console affordances: expected cost delta, reservoir health, and opt-out toggles; prepare FAQ and support KB
notes_for_engineering: Allocator prototype should expose metrics: reservoir_fill_rate, reservoir_drain_rate, avg_residency_time
Plan for KV-cache warmup API hooks to minimize end-to-end cold-start impact
Define a graceful fallback mode that prefers narrower model variants before spilling to on-demand (costly) capacity
customer_notes: Target customers for pilot: three large SaaS customers with predictable weekly release spikes and explicit latency SLAs
Pilot success criteria include 99.95% availability on reserved paths during simulated launch windows and <6% incremental monthly bill impact
